It reports at least one whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrast comparing substance users versus controls (Analysis 23072363_analysis_0: Healthy Controls > Alcohol-Dependent Patients), meeting I3. Results are reported with thresholding and peak coordinates in tables, acceptable under I4. Participant age/sex and substance-use details are reported though MRI field strength and preprocessing software are not specified in the record; per I5 missing some details alone should not exclude the study. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only or non-empirical) apply.

Record reports empirical human MRI voxelwise structural analyses of grey matter volume comparing smokers (nicotine dependence) and healthy non-smokers, including whole-brain between-group contrasts (non-smokers > light smokers; non-smokers > heavy smokers) and reported coordinate tables. Participant demographics and scanning/preprocessing details are provided in the record. Thus full-text inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5 are met. No full-text exclusion criteria (E5,E6) apply.

NeuroStore record and abstract describe an empirical structural MRI study in English assessing gray matter volume in cocaine users and controls (I2). The abstract explicitly reports gray matter volume decreases in active cocaine users relative to controls and the record shows a voxelwise model fit over the whole brain with reported peak coordinates, which supports I3 and I4. The NeuroStore extraction includes a cross-subject regression analysis rather than an explicit users<controls contrast in the listed analysis, but the abstract and reported peak(s) clearly indicate whole-brain voxelwise GM results comparing users and controls. I5 (reporting of participant and MRI details) is largely present in the record. No exclusion criteria from E5 or E6 are indicated in the record.

Record indicates an empirical MRI study of GM morphology in alcohol-dependent patients vs controls (meets I2). However, the only reported analysis is fitted and inferred over a region of interest with small-volume correction (SVC/RFT-based FWE), so no voxelwise whole-brain between-group GM contrast is reported (fails I3). I4 and I5 are satisfied or not contradictory in the record. Because the paper reports only ROI/SVC results with no qualifying whole-brain results, exclusion criterion E5 applies. Inclusion criterion I3 is not met.

Record shows an ROI-based grey matter volume analysis and whole-brain functional (BOLD) analyses but no voxelwise whole-brain GM volume comparison between substance users and controls; therefore full-text inclusion criterion I3 (whole-brain GM between-group contrast) is not met. Inclusion I2 (empirical MRI GM comparison) is met. Exclusion E5 (only ROI analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results) applies.

Record describes an empirical VBM study in English reporting voxelwise whole-brain GM volume comparisons between substance-using (alcohol-dependent, pure and polysubstance) groups and healthy controls (meets I2, I3). Peaks are reported in tables (I4). Participant demographics and scan timing are provided (I5). No ROI-only or non-empirical study indicators; no exclusion criteria met.

The NeuroStore record reports an empirical structural MRI study in English assessing cortical thickness (a grey-matter structural morphometry measure) between smokers and never-smokers (I2). Analyses are reported as whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference with reported peak coordinates, satisfying whole-brain between-group voxelwise reporting (I3, I4). Participant demographics and screening are reported (I5). No exclusion criteria (E5, E6) apply based on the record.

The NeuroStore record (title and abstract) describes an empirical VBM MRI study comparing alcohol-dependent individuals and healthy controls and reports widespread reduced gray matter volume in alcoholics (meets I2 and implies a whole-brain between-group comparison, meeting I3). Coordinate/voxelwise results appear to be reported (I4). Participant and MRI details are provided in the record (I5). The record does, however, also show that the extracted analyses provided are ROI-based within-group regressions and do not include explicit between-group whole-brain contrasts in the analysis list; this is an analysis-level ambiguity but does not by itself make the full text unreadable. No exclusion criteria (E5, E6) are met in the record.

The NeuroStore record reports an empirical VBM study in English comparing regular cannabis users to occasional smokers with whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts and reported coordinates in tables. This meets I2 (empirical MRI GM comparison), I3 (at least one whole-brain between-group GM contrast), I4 (voxelwise results reported in tables), and I5 (participant demographics and analysis software reported). No exclusion criteria (E5, E6) are met.

NeuroStore record reports voxelwise cross-subject regression analyses relating continuous measures of alcohol (AUDIT) and cannabis use to GM volume (associations), not whole-brain between-group contrasts comparing substance users versus controls. Therefore full-text inclusion criteria I2 (GM volume differences between substance users and controls) and I3 (at least one whole-brain between-group contrast of substance users vs controls) are not met. The record does show whole-brain analyses (so E5 ROI-only exclusion does not apply) and the paper is empirical (E6 does not apply).

The NeuroStore record (title and abstract) describes an empirical MRI study of gray matter volume in alcohol-dependent patients and controls, and explicitly states that the PreAction subgroup had gray matter volume deficits compared with controls (meets I2 and I3). Voxelwise whole-brain results are indicated in the record (reported peaks/tables), so I4 is also satisfied. The record includes necessary MRI and participant details although some specifics in extracted analyses are limited. No exclusion criteria (E5/E6) are met by the record.

I2 met: this is an empirical MRI study assessing GM volume differences. I4 met: voxelwise whole-brain results are reported as coordinates/tables. I3 NOT met: the NeuroStore record shows only within-group voxelwise regression/association analyses (cross-subject regressions) and does not report any whole-brain between-group contrast comparing substance users versus controls, which is required. Therefore the study is excluded for failing I3.

The NeuroStore record describes an empirical structural MRI (morphometric) study comparing adolescents with alcohol use disorders and light/non-drinking controls, reporting whole-brain voxelwise morphometric analyses (model fit over: whole brain) and between-group contrasts. Thus it meets I2 (empirical MRI GM volume comparison) and I3 (reports whole-brain between-group GM contrasts). The record includes reported peaks/tables consistent with voxelwise results, satisfying I4. I5 (additional reporting details) is optional and not required. No exclusion criteria (E5, E6) apply based on the record.

NeuroStore record indicates all reported analyses used region-of-interest model fitting and inference with small-volume correction (ROI/SVC) restricted to predefined regions (orbitofrontal cortex, anterior cingulate, striatum, amygdala, hippocampus, cerebellum). The study is an empirical VBM MRI study comparing heavy cannabis users and controls (I2 met) and qualifying voxelwise results can be reported in tables/figures (I4 met). Exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only study with no whole-brain results) applies, so the study is excluded.

Study is an empirical English-language VBM MRI study comparing grey matter volume between adolescents with alcohol use disorder and matched controls, reports whole-brain voxelwise results (model fit and inference over whole brain) with coordinate tables/peaks, and provides participant demographics and scanner/preprocessing details in the NeuroStore record. Meets I2, I3, I4 and I5. No exclusion criteria (E5, E6) apply based on the record.

NeuroStore record reports only within-group voxelwise regressions in stimulant-dependent patients (associations with severity and abstinence). Study reports an empirical structural MRI morphometric comparison of smokers vs never-smokers (grey matter density). No exclusion criteria (E5, E6) apply.

The NeuroStore record shows the study includes structural morphometry analysis (analysis_10) comparing alcohol-dependent patients and healthy controls, but the morphometry inference is restricted to a region-of-interest with small-volume correction (FWE SVC). Therefore the study reports only ROI/SVC morphometric results and lacks a qualifying whole-brain GM between-group contrast. Inclusion I2 (empirical MRI GM study) is met; I3 is not met. Exclusion E5 (studies that report only ROI analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results) applies.

The NeuroStore record reports an empirical MRI morphometry study (gray matter volume) with patients (AUD) and healthy participants and reports whole-brain analyses/peaks (I2 and I4 met). Therefore full-text inclusion criterion I3 is not met.

Record indicates an empirical structural MRI VBM study comparing methamphetamine-dependent participants to healthy controls (I2).
